text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The Pakistan foreign ministry expressed dismay at the Indian foreign secretary's statement in New Dehli about the future talks on Jamuu and Kashmir dispute and hoped that any "attempt at this stage to pre-judge or prejudice the eventual task" should be avoided.

- India has liberalised visa procedures for Pakistani nationals, easing travel for businessmen, journalists, students and artists and increasing the number of cities they could visit to 12 from eight.
- The National Assembly (lower house) passed the budget of over 552 billion rupees for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
- Sectarian violence continued unabated for the second day in Lahore when a prayer leader was shot dead on the Jail Road.
- The Supreme Court has said that the government must lay down parameter for the working of the Inter-Services Intelligence's political cell created in 1975.

- The Anti-Narcotics force, in collaboration with their colleagues in the U.S. Consulate, seized 580 kg of heroin during a raid on an apartment in Karachi's Clifton area and arrested two alleged drug traffickers.
- Two sponsors have applied for listing of new issues on the Karachi Stock Exchange, the first applications for six months.
- All items found harmful to local industry will incur 45 percent import duty, the top rate.
- The Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) has lost prospective net income of 10.5 billion rupees due to delays in the completion of various power projects.
- Four foreign banks signed a 1.19 billion rupee syndicated financing for WAPDA, with Societe Generale and ABN-AMRO Bank co-leading it.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- United Bank Limited has announced formation of five committees to accelerate revival of sick industrial units.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said corrupt elements would be punished and looted money recovered.
- The government is considering new defection laws which will provide no legal remedy for legislators unseated by their party head.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has set up a seven-member committee of legislators to review a draft constitutional amendment against floor-crossing by assembly members.
THE NATION
- The prime minister's information adviser Mushahid Hussain told the Senate that local bodies polls would be held this year.
